tex_content.html:
Proposition
[symmetries of the curvature]

↗ def:dc-ch4-2-1 ↗ prop:dc-ch4-2-4 ↗ def:dc-ch2-3-4 ↗ cor:dc-ch2-3-3

1. ch4:2.5Write $\langle R(X,Y)Z,T angle =(X,Y,Z,T)$. Then

  1. $(X,Y,Z,T)+(Y,Z,X,T)+(Z,X,Y,T)=0$;

  2. $(X,Y,Z,T)=-(Y,X,Z,T)$;

  3. $(X,Y,Z,T)=-(X,Y,T,Z)$;

  4. $(X,Y,Z,T)=(Z,T,X,Y)$.

Proof

\sketch (a) is just the Bianchi identity again; (b) follows directly from section 1; (c) is equivalent to $(X,Y,Z,Z)=0$, whose proof follows:

\[ (X,Y,Z,Z)=\langle abla _Y abla _X Z- abla _X abla _Y Z+ abla _{[X,Y]}Z,Z angle . \]

But

\[ \langle abla _Y abla _X Z,Z angle =Y\langle abla _X Z,Z angle -\langle abla _X Z, abla _Y Z angle ,\qquad \langle abla _{[X,Y]}Z,Z angle = frac {1}{2}[X,Y]\langle Z,Z angle . \]

Hence

\[ egin{aligned} (X,Y,Z,Z)& =Y\langle abla _X Z,Z angle -X\langle abla _Y Z,Z angle + frac {1}{2}[X,Y]\langle Z,Z angle \ & = frac {1}{2}Y(X\langle Z,Z angle )- frac {1}{2}X(Y\langle Z,Z angle )+ frac {1}{2}[X,Y]\langle Z,Z angle \ & =- frac {1}{2}[X,Y]\langle Z,Z angle + frac {1}{2}[X,Y]\langle Z,Z angle =0,\end{aligned} \]

which proves (c). To prove (d), we use (a), and write:

\[ egin{aligned} (X,Y,Z,T)+(Y,Z,X,T)+(Z,X,Y,T)& =0,\ (Y,Z,T,X)+(Z,T,Y,X)+(T,Y,Z,X)& =0,\ (Z,T,X,Y)+(T,X,Z,Y)+(X,Z,T,Y)& =0,\ (T,X,Y,Z)+(X,Y,T,Z)+(Y,T,X,Z)& =0.\end{aligned} \]

Summing the equations above we obtain $2(Z,X,Y,T)+2(T,Y,Z,X)=0$ and therefore $(Z,X,Y,T)=(Y,T,Z,X)$. $ lacksquare $
